# Metric Kind

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:MetricKind`](gmeow-MetricKind.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/MetricKind>
- **Category:** class
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/places`](../../slices/places.md)
- **Box roles:** [TBox role](../boxes/tbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The computational method by which distance or dissimilarity is measured in a reference frame — geodesic (curved surface), Euclidean (straight-line in Cartesian space), cosine (angular similarity in latent vector space), edit-distance (Levenshtein / sequence alignment), or graph-hops (shortest-path in a network). A value vocabulary (individuals, never subclasses) per [Principle 9](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-9).

## Structure

**Subclass of:** [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:MetricKind`](gmeow-MetricKind.md) as a specialized kind of [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue). Add statement metadata or a standpoint when the assertion needs provenance, confidence, or vantage.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to name how distance or dissimilarity is computed in a frame — geodesic, Euclidean, cosine, edit-distance, graph-hops — as a value individual.

### Avoid when

- Avoid materialising the computed distances as triples (the metric declares the method; the solver computes, [Principle 12](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-12)) and avoid subclassing for a new metric.

### How to use

- Mint the metric as a [`gmeow:MetricKind`](gmeow-MetricKind.md) individual and reference it from a frame via the functional [`gmeow:hasMetricKind`](../properties/gmeow-hasMetricKind.md).

### Examples

- ex:metricGeodesic a [`gmeow:MetricKind`](gmeow-MetricKind.md).
